newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco to study oxide deposit at Chuquicamata.
newsitem.headline: Codelco to study oxide deposit at Chuquicamata.

text.p: Chile's state-owned copper company Codelco will begin a pre-feasibility study next year for developing a deposit north of the Chuquicamata mine believed to hold a "reasonable" amount of copper, said a top official.
The tract, known as Chuqui Norte, could be producing cathodes in about 2003, said the general manager of Codelco's Chuquicamata mine, Nelson Pizarro.
"It's called Chuqui Norte and in fact it could be suitable for heap-leaching cathodes," he told reporters.
The size, mineral grade and depth of the deposit are still unknown, he said.
"The area is under exploration...and pretty soon we'll know what its magnitude is," he said.
"It's probably of a reasonable size," he said.
The deposit has oxides suitable for heap-leaching and probably holds sulphides lower down, said Pizarro.
"For the year 2003 we could have production of cathodes," he said, adding that Codelco envisions Chuqui Norte replacing part of declining output at Chuquicamata's Mina Sur pit.
Codelco has long suspected that the area, lying between Chuquicamata and the Radomiro Tomic project, contained viable copper reserves but recently stepped up exploration.
"We've known it all along, we known it for 50 years that there were (copper) resources there. The idea that there is copper there is nothing new," said Pizarro.
He stressed that Codelco had no new discovery to report at Chuqui Norte or any other deposit.
Codelco has been stepping up exploration to help make up for stagnant grades at some of its four major mines.
A pre-feasibility study usually involves a basic preliminary look at a deposit's commercial potential and does not necessary mean the tract will be commercially developed.
